author: josh1125
text: Ok..it's time for me to wake my journal back up...I've come such a long way over the past few months, and I finally feel like I'm at the place to where I can finally give back. Here is my read on the eurusd at the moment. It's clear to see that shorts are out of play right now, unless you're going to scalp shorts. All target for shorts have been hit. We had a nice move out of the origin, then we had a nice reaction from the edge of our CPAZ..now we're pretty much waiting to see what it is price wants to do. I see two scenarios that could play out here. The first scenario is price could engulf into PAZ 2 then retrace to our fresh FL before heading north. The second could be a engulf into PAZ 1, then an engulf of PAZ 2 before returning to the FTR limiting PAZ 1 before a move up. The second scenario is what I feel is more likely to happen. As of now, all we can really do is sit back and wait for PA to show us the way.

author: josh1125
text: Since my work schedule pretty much forces me to trade HTF, I am waiting to pull the trigger on the audusd. I'm expecting to get a sell order at the FO level. As I learned from Dr. Swing's journal, whenever an FTR is within 30 pips of a fresh FO level, always expect price to FO. So I'm going to place a pending sell at the FO level, and if I miss the trade oh well, but I'm feeling very confident that my order will be filled. I've seen this scenario multiple times in the charts.

author: victoryong
text: Quick question Josh1125, do you mean that if two FTR is located within 30pips of each other, there is a chance that the 2nd FTR will be a FO level? I'm assuming that the first FTR is an important one.

author: josh1125
text:
Victoryong, Let me rephrase that a little differently. Whenever you have a fresh FL near an FTR, we should always expect price to FO to the fresh FL. When thinking in like an IT, we want to get in at the best possible price. In the chart below, we see we our FTR formed, after the engulf. We can see above the FTR there was a fresh FL. Price FO'd our FTR and entered the fresh FL above before breaking down. This is seem time and time again in the charts. Whenever there is a FRESH FL in close proximity of an FTR always expect price to FO. The key here is that the area we are expecting price to FO to has to be fresh.

author: josh1125
text:
Sorry it took me so long to get back to you. The origin of the move is simply the first FTR in a move. When placing a TP, I normally TP at the next opposite FTR/FL. I marked up a quick chart showing the way I read price. In the chart below you can see in the initial down move, several bullish FTRs were engulfed. Once price decided to turn around without reaching it's target, we would have entered a sell at the origin, and our TP would have been the FTR that price was initially attracted to but never reached. Remember, the space between FTRs are a type of PAZ. So when price enters a PAZ it's going to go to the opposing side. Hope this helps a little.
